description: #3830 — READ-command differential over `list_peer_refs`, waived as "peer registry (device metadata) outside the conformance snapshot scope" until a fixture could put the same rows on both stacks; `seed.peer_refs` is that, every column the command selects inserted verbatim into the backend `peer_refs` table and the mock's map (`loro_vv_bytes` is not selected and is not seeded). The seed exists to make ORDER discriminate: `peer_refs::list_peer_refs` is `ORDER BY synced_at DESC`, and SQLite sorts NULLs LAST under DESC, so the three rows are seeded in the REVERSE of that order — the never-synced peer first, then the older sync, then the newest — and the ordered comparison pins the sort rather than insertion order, which was one divergence this fixture found and fixed in the mock; the other was two columns (`endpoint_id`, `unpaired_by_peer_at_ms`) the mock's row never carried. The `synced_at` values are distinct on purpose: a tie's order is not something `ORDER BY` promises, so no step pins one. Every other nullable column is null on at least one row and set on at least one other, so a column dropped or mis-mapped on either stack reddens. Peer ids, hashes and names are short fixture labels; `endpoint_id` is 64 hex characters because migration 0107's CHECK demands it. The local device's own `peer_id = ''` sentinel row is not seeded: the command's WHERE hides it, and no mock path ever writes one. NOT pinned: `delete_peer_ref`, `update_peer_name`, `set_peer_address` (mutating peer commands, still waived).
name: query_peer_refs

queries.comment: `peer-new` (synced 2000), then `peer-old` (1000), then `peer-never` (`synced_at` null) — the reverse of the seed order. Insertion order, or an ascending sort, or NULLs-first, each redden. Every token carries all twelve non-id columns, so the two columns the mock's row lacked (`endpoint_id`, `unpaired_by_peer_at_ms`) and every null/non-null pairing are pinned too.
queries.name: peer_refs_synced_at_desc_nulls_last
